structured_output.summary: Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(3)(b), checked again, gives a refundable credit equal to 20% of the federal § 32 EITC for taxable years from January 1, 2025 through before January 1, 2027, so it applies to 2026. The head is 40, single, has no children and has no investment income. They get a federal EITC of 7.65% × $520 = $39.78, still in the phase-in. Virginia tax is $0, so the refundable option is the right one. The engine took 20% × $39.78 = $7.956, which matches the law. The 25-model consensus of $0 is wrong: the refundable credit did not expire before 2026, and childless EITC phases in from the first dollar earned.

The 2026 EIC table had not been published by the 2026-07-03 freeze, so the only pre-freeze way to get the amount is the § 32(a) formula ($39.78, so $7.96). This is not a substantive error.
